name: Aseptic personnel qualification and gowning check
purpose: Gate entry to and work in Grade A/B aseptic operations on current gowning qualification, aseptic-behaviour training and successful APS participation.
config_options: qualification types required per room grade/operation (gowning qualification, aseptic technique, intervention-specific training, APS participation)
requalification intervals from the site CCS (e.g. annual gowning reassessment, APS participation within the defined period)
integration with access control/training system
visual gowning check at entry (checklist) and post-session glove/gown monitoring link
engine_enforced_rules: a person without current gowning qualification and APS participation cannot be recorded as performing or intervening in Grade A/B aseptic steps
qualification status snapshot is stored with each aseptic action
personnel monitoring results (glove/gown prints) are linked to the person and session and flow into EM review for the batch
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 7 (personnel: gowning qualification, reassessment at least annually, unsupervised Grade A/B access only after gowning assessment and successful APS); 21 CFR 211.25, 211.28; FDA aseptic processing guidance (2004)

name: Environmental and personnel monitoring linkage
purpose: Link the batch to viable and non-viable monitoring of its processing sessions (settle plates, active air, contact plates, glove prints, continuous particle counts) so results are part of batch review.
config_options: EM plan per room/line and session (locations, sample types, frequencies) referenced from the EM system
session boundaries (start/end of filling, interventions)
alert/action levels by grade (from EM system)
which results are required before batch disposition (incubated plate reads)
engine_enforced_rules: EM samples for each session are created/linked automatically when the session starts; missing samples are exceptions
Grade A continuous particle monitoring data for the session window is imported and excursions become exceptions
batch disposition is blocked until all linked EM results (including incubated plates) are available and excursions dispositioned
EM trend data for the period is presented in the batch review package
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 9 (EM; continuous Grade A particle monitoring; EM trend data reviewed as part of batch certification/release); 21 CFR 211.42(c)(10)(iv), 211.113(b); FDA aseptic processing guidance (2004)

name: Compounding with WFI and pH/volume adjustment
purpose: Prepare the bulk solution/suspension: WFI addition, dissolution of components, pH adjustment loop, make-up to final weight/volume, in-process checks.
config_options: WFI use point, required WFI temperature/quality release status
order and rate of additions, mixing speed/time, temperature, nitrogen sparging/blanketing
pH target and limits, adjusting agents and maximum cumulative additions
final make-up basis (weight with density, or volume)
IPC: pH, density, appearance/clarity, assay/osmolality via LIMS
start of compounding-to-filtration time-limit clock
engine_enforced_rules: WFI loop/use point status must be released (no active excursion) at time of draw
each pH adjustment iteration is recorded; exceeding the maximum adjusting agent quantity raises an exception
final quantity computed and checked by the engine (weight/density/volume conversions)
compounding start event automatically starts the chained time limits to filtration and filling
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.101, 211.110(a)(5)-(6) (solution clarity/completeness/pH; bioburden), 211.111; EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8; FDA aseptic processing guidance (2004) time limits

name: Pre-filtration bioburden sampling
purpose: Sample the bulk immediately before sterilising filtration for bioburden (and endotoxin where required), with results linked to disposition.
config_options: sample volume, point and timing relative to filtration start
limit (from filter validation/registration)
LIMS test mapping
engine_enforced_rules: filtration cannot start before the bioburden sample is recorded
result is linked to the batch; disposition blocked until available; a result above limit raises an exception
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110(a)(6), 211.113(b); EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8 (bioburden before sterilisation/filtration); FDA aseptic processing guidance (2004)

name: Sterilising filtration with filter integrity testing (PUPSIT and post-use)
purpose: Execute sterilising-grade filtration and prove filter integrity before use (after sterilisation) and after use, with integrity-tester data captured.
config_options: filter/assembly type and validated filter part numbers
integrity test method (bubble point, diffusion/forward flow, pressure hold, water intrusion) and product-/wetting-fluid-specific limits
PUPSIT required, or not applicable with reference to an approved risk assessment
redundant filter configuration and which filter is tested
filtration parameters: max differential pressure, flow, max filtration time, max volume/throughput
engine_enforced_rules: filter and housing IDs scanned; part number must match validated list; filter must be within sterilisation hold time
pre-use (post-sterilisation) integrity test must pass before product filtration starts unless the MBR carries a QA-approved PUPSIT justification
post-use non-destructive integrity test is mandatory before the filter is removed from its housing; a failure raises a critical exception and blocks disposition
integrity test results imported from the tester with instrument ID, test parameters and raw values; manual transcription only as flagged fallback with verification
filtration time and differential pressure limits enforced
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) section 8.87 (PUPSIT; post-use integrity test); 21 CFR 211.113(b); FDA aseptic processing guidance (2004) on filtration efficacy and integrity testing

name: Sterilisation cycle record (autoclave / SIP) for equipment and components
purpose: Record each sterilisation run of equipment, change parts, filters, stoppers or garments: load, validated cycle, cycle data, indicators, and resulting sterile-hold expiry.
config_options: steriliser class and validated cycle IDs allowed per load type
load pattern reference (validated loading configuration) and item list per load
cycle parameters to capture (temperature, pressure, time at temperature, F0, drying) and acceptance limits
biological/chemical indicator use and result capture
sterile hold time per item type and wrapping/protection method
engine_enforced_rules: only validated cycle IDs for the declared load pattern can be selected
cycle data imported from the steriliser controller/SCADA with cycle number; the cycle report is attached; a failed or aborted cycle cannot yield 'sterile' status
items get a sterile status with a sterile-hold expiry computed by the engine; expired or unsterile items are blocked from use in aseptic steps
sterilisation records are presented for review as part of batch disposition
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8 (sterilisation: records per run reviewed for batch release; BIs unless parametric release authorised; defined storage time for sterilised items); 21 CFR 211.113(b), 211.67; FDA aseptic processing guidance (2004) time limits for sterilised equipment/containers/closures

name: Depyrogenation (dry-heat tunnel or oven)
purpose: Depyrogenate and sterilise glass containers (vials, ampoules, cartridges) or other heat-stable items, capturing the validated time-temperature profile.
config_options: tunnel/oven class and validated programme per container format
belt speed, hot-zone temperature, cooling-zone parameters and differential pressures
acceptance limits and data capture interval
hold time of depyrogenated containers before filling
engine_enforced_rules: only the validated programme for the container format can be used; format mismatch blocks
temperature/belt-speed/pressure excursions during the run raise exceptions and identify affected containers/time window
depyrogenated containers inherit an expiry; filling with expired containers is blocked
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8 (dry heat sterilisation/depyrogenation); Ph. Eur. 5.1.2/2.6.8 context; 21 CFR 211.94(c), 211.113(b)

name: Primary component preparation and RTU/nested component acceptance
purpose: Prepare stoppers, seals and containers (washing, siliconisation, sterilisation) or accept ready-to-use (RTU) sterile nested tubs/bags for vials, cartridges and prefilled syringes, including transfer decontamination into Grade A.
config_options: component type and preparation route (in-house wash/sterilise vs RTU)
RTU acceptance checks: supplier sterilisation certificate/lot release, bag/tub integrity, expiry
transfer method into the isolator/RABS (e-beam tunnel, VHP pass-box, decontaminated bag port) and its cycle record
count/quantity per tub and reconciliation
engine_enforced_rules: RTU lots must be released by QA and within expiry; integrity check of outer packaging recorded before transfer
transfer decontamination cycle must be completed and passed before components enter Grade A
component quantities feed reconciliation of filled units
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapters 5 and 8 (transfer of materials into Grade A, sterilisation of components); 21 CFR 211.84, 211.94, 211.113(b)

name: Isolator/RABS decontamination and glove integrity
purpose: Record bio-decontamination cycles (e.g. VHP) of isolators/RABS and glove/sleeve integrity testing around each batch.
config_options: validated decontamination cycle IDs per enclosure
cycle parameters and indicators (chemical/biological) captured
glove integrity test method (physical leak test, visual check) and frequency (at least start and end of batch/campaign; visual checks per session)
action on failed glove test (impact assessment on units filled since last pass)
engine_enforced_rules: aseptic filling cannot start in an enclosure without a passed decontamination cycle within its validity
glove integrity tests are scheduled at the configured points; a failed or missed test raises an exception and flags units filled since the last passing test
glove/port IDs recorded with results
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 4 (glove integrity testing at least at the beginning and end of each batch or campaign; decontamination of isolators); 21 CFR 211.113(b)

name: Sterile process time-limit chain
purpose: Enforce the chained, validated time limits of sterile manufacture across unit procedures (compounding start to filtration end, filtration to filling end, sterile hold of equipment/components, product exposure on line, fill to lyophilisation/stoppering, fill to terminal sterilisation).
config_options: time-limit definitions (start event, stop event, maximum, alert) linked to CCS/validation references
which limits block downstream steps vs raise exception only
display of all running clocks for the batch on a single supervisor view
engine_enforced_rules: all clocks run on server time from recorded events; users cannot enter elapsed times
any exceeded maximum raises an exception; configured blocking limits prevent the next step until QA disposition
time-limit values must cite the supporting validation/hold study in the MBR before approval
all clock results appear in the review-by-exception report
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.111; FDA Sterile Drug Products Produced by Aseptic Processing guidance (2004) (time limits incl. compounding to sterilisation, filtration, exposure on line, storage of sterilised items); EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8

name: Aseptic filling set-up and fill weight/volume control
purpose: Set up the filling line (format parts, pumps/needles) aseptically and control fill quantity by periodic or 100% in-process weighing, per filling needle.
config_options: container format (vial, ampoule, cartridge, syringe) and format parts IDs
filling system (piston, peristaltic, time-pressure) and number of needles
target fill (weight via density, or volume) with limits per unit and mean; extractable-volume basis
check frequency per needle (start, periodic, after adjustment, end) or 100% in-line checkweighing
adjustment rules and who may adjust
first-units discard quantity at start/restart
engine_enforced_rules: fill weights captured from the (IPC) balance or line checkweigher per needle with timestamps; manual entry flagged and verified
out-of-limit fill triggers exception and reject/hold of units since the last passing check for that needle
every fill adjustment is recorded with before/after values, user and time
units rejected for fill feed reconciliation automatically
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110(a), 211.113(b); EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8; USP <697>/<1151> (container content/extractable volume) as method context

name: Aseptic interventions log
purpose: Record every inherent and corrective intervention in Grade A during aseptic processing, checked against the list of interventions qualified by APS.
config_options: site list of approved interventions (inherent vs corrective) with the APS that qualified each
required details per intervention (who, when, duration, location, units removed, line clearance of affected units)
automatic capture from line events (door open, line stop) where interfaced
classification rules for unplanned interventions
engine_enforced_rules: an intervention not on the APS-qualified list is flagged as an unplanned intervention and raises an exception requiring QA assessment
the performer must hold current qualification for that intervention
line-event data (e.g. RABS door openings) without a matching recorded intervention become exceptions
units to be removed after an intervention are recorded and reconciled
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) sections 8.16-8.18 (list of interventions evaluated by QRM and APS; recorded in batch documentation) and 9.34 (APS covers inherent and corrective interventions); FDA aseptic processing guidance (2004)

name: Stoppering, capping/crimping with missing-stopper rejection
purpose: Control stopper placement and cap/crimp application, rejecting containers with missing or displaced stoppers before capping and checking seal quality.
config_options: stopper height/presence sensor settings (qualified) and challenge frequency
capping location type (Grade A air supply, isolator) and technology
crimp quality checks (visual, residual seal force if used) and frequency
reject verification challenges
engine_enforced_rules: missing/raised-stopper detection must be active and its challenge passed before capping starts; failed challenge stops the step
rejected containers are counted and cannot re-enter the good stream
crimp checks are scheduled; failures hold output since last good check
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8 (containers with missing or displaced stoppers rejected before capping; capping under Grade A air supply); 21 CFR 211.94

name: Lyophilisation cycle (loading, cycle record, stoppering, unloading)
purpose: Record transfer and loading of partially stoppered containers, the validated freeze-drying cycle, in-chamber stoppering and unloading.
config_options: lyophiliser class and validated cycle recipe IDs per product/fill
loading method (automatic loading system, transfer carts under Grade A) and documented loading pattern
cycle phases and parameters (freezing, primary/secondary drying shelf temperature, chamber pressure, durations), endpoint tests (pressure rise, comparative pressure)
stoppering pressure/gas (nitrogen backfill), chamber sterilisation before load where required
maximum time from filling to start of cycle
engine_enforced_rules: the cycle recipe downloaded is the validated one for the product and read back; recipe edits at the controller are captured and raised as exceptions
transfer and loading steps record Grade A conditions/equipment; loading pattern captured
full cycle trend and alarm list are imported; alarms configured as critical block disposition until assessed
lyophiliser sterilisation status before load is checked where the design requires it (e.g. manual loading without barrier separation)
time limit from filling to cycle start enforced
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) sections 8.122-8.126 (lyophilisation: transfer of partially closed containers under Grade A, loading pattern documented, sterilisation of manually loaded lyophilisers); 21 CFR 211.113(b), 211.111

name: Terminal sterilisation of filled product
purpose: Sterilise sealed containers (typically moist heat) using a validated load and cycle, and record cycle data, indicators and load segregation.
config_options: validated cycle and load pattern per product/container
parameters and limits (temperature, time, F0, pressure/air-over-pressure)
BI/CI placement and results, or parametric release profile where authorised
segregation of sterilised vs non-sterilised loads (status/scan)
maximum time from filling to sterilisation
engine_enforced_rules: only validated cycle/load combinations can be used; cycle data imported and evaluated against limits
a load cannot be marked sterilised without a passing cycle record (and BI results unless parametric release is authorised)
scanning prevents non-sterilised trays from entering the sterilised area/status
fill-to-sterilisation time limit enforced
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8 (terminal sterilisation, BIs unless parametric release authorised); EU GMP Annex 17 (real-time release/parametric release); 21 CFR 211.113(b), 211.167(a)

name: 100% visual inspection and post-inspection AQL
purpose: Record 100% inspection of filled units (manual, semi-automated or automated) with defect classification and counts, followed by acceptance sampling (AQL) of the accepted units.
config_options: inspection mode per product/container (manual booth, semi-automated, automated with validated recipe)
defect library and classes (critical/major/minor; particles, cosmetic, container, closure, fill)
inspector qualification requirements and maximum continuous inspection period before a break
automated inspection recipe ID and challenge (known-defect set) at start/end
AQL sampling plan and acceptance numbers per defect class
reject rate alert/action limits (trend-based) triggering investigation
engine_enforced_rules: only inspectors with current qualification (incl. eyesight check) can record manual inspection; session duration is tracked against the break rule
automated machine must use the validated recipe and pass the challenge set; recipe change during run is an exception
defect counts by class feed reconciliation: inspected = accepted + rejected by class (+ samples)
AQL failure blocks disposition and triggers exception (re-inspection only via approved procedure)
reject rates above limits raise exceptions for investigation
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) sections 8.30-8.33 (100% inspection; inspector qualification, eyesight checks, breaks; automated inspection validated to be at least as good as manual; defects recorded and trended); USP <790>/<1790> (100% inspection followed by acceptance sampling, AQL 0.65% for visible particles); 21 CFR 211.110, 211.192

name: Container closure integrity testing (in-process)
purpose: Test seal integrity of filled containers: 100% for fusion-sealed small containers (ampoules, BFS) and by sampling for other container types, using validated (preferably deterministic) methods.
config_options: container type and whether 100% testing is mandatory (fusion-sealed, small volume) or sampling (with justified plan)
method (HVLD, vacuum decay, laser headspace, pressure decay; dye ingress only where justified)
instrument/recipe ID and challenge with positive controls
sampling frequency and sample size where not 100%
engine_enforced_rules: for fusion-sealed small-volume containers the MBR cannot be approved without a 100% integrity test step
visual inspection cannot be configured as the integrity test method
test results and rejects imported from the tester with recipe and challenge results; failed challenge holds output since last good challenge
rejected units counted into reconciliation
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) sections 8.22-8.25 (100% integrity testing of fusion-sealed containers such as ampoules/BFS/small containers; visual inspection not an acceptable integrity method); USP <1207>; 21 CFR 211.94

name: Aseptic process simulation (media fill) execution and reconciliation
purpose: Run an APS as a special batch type from a dedicated MBR variant: growth medium replaces product, worst-case conditions and planned interventions are executed, and every unit is reconciled through incubation and reading.
config_options: APS MBR variant linked to the commercial process it qualifies (line, container, shift, maximum duration, maximum number of personnel)
planned worst-case interventions list and schedule
medium, fill volume, container orientation/inversion, incubation temperatures and durations
personnel participating (for their qualification records)
growth promotion test link
engine_enforced_rules: APS records are clearly typed as APS and can never be released as product
every filled unit is accounted for: filled = incubated + justified discards (e.g. integrity failures) with reasons; unexplained differences are exceptions
any contaminated unit marks the APS failed and triggers investigation; results update line and personnel qualification status automatically
planned interventions not performed, or unplanned ones performed, are highlighted
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) sections 9.32-9.49 (APS design, interventions, incubation and reconciliation of all units, zero-growth target; personnel qualification); FDA aseptic processing guidance (2004) media fill section; 21 CFR 211.113(b)

name: Sterility and endotoxin sampling linked to fill events
purpose: Take finished-product sterility (and endotoxin) samples that represent the batch, including beginning, end and after significant interventions, and link them to LIMS.
config_options: sampling points (start, end, after specific interventions or line stops, per lyophiliser/steriliser load)
number of units per point from the pharmacopoeial/registered sampling plan
LIMS test mapping and result dependencies for disposition
engine_enforced_rules: event-driven samples (e.g. after a corrective intervention) are requested automatically when the event is recorded
sample units are removed from the good count and appear in reconciliation
disposition is blocked until sterility/endotoxin results are received (unless an authorised parametric release applies to sterility)
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.167(a), 211.165; EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 10 (sterility test samples representative incl. after interventions); Ph. Eur. 2.6.1 / USP <71>

name: Filled-unit reconciliation across filling, lyophilisation, inspection and CCI
purpose: Reconcile containers from component issue through filling, closing, lyophilisation/sterilisation, visual inspection, CCI and sampling, per stage and overall.
config_options: stages and the unit categories counted at each (issued containers, filled, fill rejects, intervention removals, stoppering/capping rejects, lyo/sterilisation losses, inspection rejects by class, CCI rejects, samples, accepted)
reconciliation tolerance per stage
source of counts (machine counters vs manual counts with verification)
engine_enforced_rules: counts from machines are imported, not typed; manual counts need verification
each stage balance must close within tolerance; unexplained differences raise exceptions blocking disposition
reject categories cannot be merged after the fact; each rejected unit class is traceable to its source step
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.103, 211.192; EU GMP Chapter 5 (reconciliation); EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) (interventions, inspection rejects recorded)

name: Process gas filtration, nitrogen overlay and headspace oxygen
purpose: Control sterile process gases (nitrogen/air for overlay, purging, pressurisation) through sterilising gas filters and verify headspace oxygen for oxygen-sensitive products.
config_options: gas filter IDs and integrity test requirement (pre/post use per CCS)
overlay/purge parameters
headspace oxygen method (laser headspace), limit, frequency
engine_enforced_rules: gas filter integrity status is checked before the gas point is used in Grade A
headspace oxygen results out of limit raise exceptions and hold units since last passing check
gas supply quality release status verified
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 6 (gases in contact with product filtered through sterilising-grade filters; integrity) and chapter 8; 21 CFR 211.113(b)

name: Single-use assembly installation and integrity
purpose: Install pre-sterilised single-use assemblies (bags, tubing, filters, connectors) for compounding, filtration and filling, verifying identity, sterility status and integrity.
config_options: validated assembly part numbers per process step
checks: supplier release/irradiation certificate, expiry, outer packaging integrity, connection method (aseptic connectors, tube welding) and weld inspection
leak/integrity test of the installed assembly where specified
engine_enforced_rules: assembly lot must be released and unexpired; part number must match the MBR
every aseptic connection/weld is recorded with performer and result
assembly integrity failures raise exceptions before product contact
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8 (single-use systems: integrity, supplier qualification, sterility assurance); 21 CFR 211.65, 211.67, 211.84

name: Prefilled syringe/cartridge closure placement
purpose: Control plunger-stopper placement (vacuum or vent-tube) and nest/tub handling for prefilled syringes and cartridges, with positional and functional checks.
config_options: placement method and parameters (vacuum level, insertion depth)
stopper position measurement (camera or gauge) and limits
optional functional IPC (break-loose/glide force) by sampling
tub/nest handling and de-lidding in Grade A
engine_enforced_rules: stopper position results captured from the inspection device; out-of-limit units rejected and counted
placement parameter excursions raise exceptions and identify affected tubs
tub/nest IDs traced from RTU acceptance to filled output
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.94, 211.110; EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8

name: Ampoule fusion sealing control
purpose: Control flame/fusion sealing parameters of glass ampoules and link to the mandatory 100% integrity test.
config_options: gas/oxygen flow settings and ranges, sealing station speed
seal appearance checks (tips, bubbles, charring) frequency
link to the downstream 100% CCI step
engine_enforced_rules: sealing parameters captured; excursions flag the affected time window
a batch of ampoules cannot be dispositioned without the 100% integrity test results
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) section 8.22 (fusion-sealed containers subject to 100% integrity testing; seal parameters controlled and monitored)

name: Cleanroom/zone release for aseptic operations
purpose: Release a Grade A/B zone for aseptic processing: completion of cleaning/disinfection (incl. sporicide rotation), pressure cascade and airflow status, non-viable monitoring status, and room/line clearance.
config_options: disinfection programme reference (agents, rotation, contact times) per room
required status inputs (BMS pressure cascade, UDAF/HEPA status, particle counter status)
room clearance checklist for aseptic areas
validity period of a room release
engine_enforced_rules: aseptic steps cannot start in a zone without a valid release; BMS/EMS alarms during the session become exceptions
disinfection records carry agent lot/expiry and are verified
room release validity expires automatically (server time) and must be renewed
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapters 4, 6 and 9 (premises, cleaning/disinfection, monitoring); 21 CFR 211.42(c)(10), 211.56, 211.113(b)
